IS : 12181 - 1987 

Indian Standard 

DETERMINATION OF COLOUR STABILITY OF 
DENTAL POLYMERIC MATERIALS 



a FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards 
on 31 August, 1987 after the draft finalized by the Dental Materials 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division 
Council. 

0.2 Colour stability is an important characteristic of dental polymeric 
materials and it is expected that the test methods in this standard will 
be referred to in the standard specifying those materials. 

0.3 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived 
from ISO 7491-1985 Dental materials — Determination of colour 
stability of dental polymeric materials. 

0.4 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with 
this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded 
off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifes a method for the determination of colour 
stability of dental polymeric materials. 

2. METHOD OF TEST 
2.1 Apparatus 

2.1.1 Radiation Source — Xeron lamp with a colour temperature of 
5 000 to 7 000°K and with an illumirance at the specimen of 150 000 lux. 
Any deviation of the illuminance from the mean value at any given 
moment shall rot exceed ± 10 percent over the entire area occupied by 
the test specimen. 

2.1.1.1 Other radiation sources of equivalent performance to the 
xenon are also suitable. 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 



IS : 12181 . 1987 



Note — The xenon lamp and the filters (2.14 ) should normally be replaced 
af er 1 500 h use because of the change of radiation intensity due to ageing. The 
iUuminance output should be calibrated with a suitable light measuring initru- 
ment such as the Haoau instrqinent. 

2 J .2 Filters 

2.1.2.1 Ultraviolet filters — Borosilicate glass filter with transmit- 
tarce of less than 1 percent below 300 nm and greater than 90 percent 
above HO nm. 

2.1.2.2 Heat Filter — Such that the temperature recorded with the 
fiUer in position will not exceed 55°C when measured by a blapk panpl 
th^rmoTneter ( see note ), or a mercury thermometer with a blackened 
buib, mounted in the position normally occupied by the test specimen. 

Note — The black panel thermometer consists of a 0-9 ± 0*1 mm thick steel 
panel the size of one specimen and finished with a black flossy enamel having 
good resistance to light. A means for measuring the temperature ofthepaniel 
is provided at the centre; a thermocoupJc or bimetallic thermometer t^.^kinf 
intimate contact with the panel iis, suitable. 

24J Test Chamber — The test chairiber comprises the folIgwin| 
components. 

2.1.3.1 Trough of circulating water r— mait|tained at 3? ± 3^€J* 
The water level is maintained at 10 ± 5 mm above the ^pecimen§ ^nd 
the specimens are held parallel to the bottom of the chamber. 

2.1.3.2 Specimen holder --r. ^ suitable holder for discs up to 50 mra 
diameter is shown in Fig, 1. 









All dimensions In miliimetres. 
Fig. 1 Holder for Specimen Discs up to 50 mm Diameter

2.2 Procedure 

2.2.1 Radiation Test — Either clamp the specimen discs with ha'f of 
each one in the holder as shown in the figure or cover one half of each 



IS : 12181 - 1987 

specimen with tin or aluminium foil. For specimen teeth, cover half of 
the vestibular surface with tin or aluminium foil parallel to the long 
axis of the tooth. 

2.2.1.1 With the filters ( 2*1.2 ) in position, expose the test specimens 
in the water bath to the radiation of the xenon lamp ( 2.1.1 ) for 24 h. 
Take care to avoid casting shadows on the specimens. 

2.2.2 Colour Comparison — Store unradiated specimen under de- 
ionized water for 24 h before comparing with the exposed specimens. 

2.2.2.1 Use three people with normal colour vision to compare by 
visual inspection the exposed and unexposed half of each of the specimens 
and the unradiated specimen for any colour differences. Make the 
comparison in bright diffuse daylight under an overcast "northern/ 
southern" sky or aUernatively, under the xenon or equivalent Inmp 
without any significant coloured reflection using a minimum illuminance 
of 1 000 lux. 

2.2.2.2 For specimen discs, place a diffused white backgro^ind of- 
reflectance 90 percent ( white bond paper is suitable ) behind the samnl- 
Limit the background to the size of the disc and surround it by a diffused 
black background felt or velvet is suitable. 

2.2.2.3 For tooth shaped specimens, use a diffused b^ack back- 
ground such as felt or velvet, 

2.2.2.4 Allow the three observers to view the specimens for aperiod 
of not longer than 2 seconds. 

2.2.2.5 Record the mean of the independent comparisons of the 
three observers.
